[8, 10, 21] The District of Columbia's minimum wage will increase to $17.95 per hour for non-tipped workers; however, a planned increase for tipped employees has been postponed. [6, 11, 12] Numerous cities in California will see increases, including Los Angeles ($17.87), San Francisco ($19.18), and others. [4, 17] In Illinois, the City of Chicago's minimum wage will increase to $16.60, but Cook County's rate will not change on this date. [4, 24] In Maryland, Montgomery County will raise its wage with rates varying by employer size, from $15.50 to $17.65. [13, 23] Lastly, in Minnesota, Saint Paul will increase its minimum wage for small and micro businesses to $15.00 and $13.25, respectively. [18, 19, 30] <7> On July 1, 2025, several cities in California will implement an increase in their minimum wage. The new hourly rates will be as follows: Berkeley will increase to $19.18, Emeryville will rise to $19.90, the City of Los Angeles to $17.87, and unincorporated areas of Los Angeles County to $17.81. Additionally, Pasadena's minimum wage will be $18.04, San Francisco's will be $19.18, and Santa Monica's will be $17.81. These local wage increases surpass California's statewide minimum wage of $16.50 per hour. Official notices regarding these changes have been published by the respective city and county governments.
